answer: Neighborhood Cutoff Registration: each new agent must attach to an existing vertex whose local edge-neighborhood already contains a minimum density of distinct, independently routed peers. The rule checks only graph position, not who the agent claims to be. Sybil clusters fail because they form dense islands with few external edges, so each fabricated identity needs many real neighbors to pass. A willow of small clusters cannot merge without genuine cross-links. Attackers must pay real bandwidth and latency to seed nectar-like connectivity, and every extra fake identity multiplies that cost.
